statement: Let k = n/2, D1 = { nums1[i] | 0 <= i < n }, and D2 = { nums2[i] | 0 <= i < n }. The function returns a result r and r = min(|D1 ∪ D2|, min(k, |D1|) + min(k, |D2|)).
preconditions: Let n = len(nums1). Assume len(nums2) = n, n is even, 1 <= n <= 20000, and 1 <= nums1[i] <= 1000000000 and 1 <= nums2[i] <= 1000000000 for every valid index i.

statement: For every input satisfying the preconditions, maximum_set_size returns a result r; it never fails, overflows, panics, or accesses out of bounds.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums1). Assume len(nums2) = n, n is even, 1 <= n <= 20000, and 1 <= nums1[i] <= 1000000000 and 1 <= nums2[i] <= 1000000000 for every valid index i.

statement: Let n = len(nums1). Whenever maximum_set_size returns r, we have 1 <= r <= n.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums1). Assume len(nums2) = n, n is even, 1 <= n <= 20000, and all array entries are between 1 and 1000000000.

statement: Let D1 = { nums1[i] | 0 <= i < n } and D2 = { nums2[i] | 0 <= i < n }. Whenever maximum_set_size returns r, we have r <= |D1 ∪ D2|.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums1). Assume len(nums2) = n, n is even, 1 <= n <= 20000, and all array entries are between 1 and 1000000000.

statement: Let k = n/2, D1 = { nums1[i] | 0 <= i < n }, and D2 = { nums2[i] | 0 <= i < n }. Whenever maximum_set_size returns r, we have r <= min(k, |D1|) + min(k, |D2|).
preconditions: Let n = len(nums1). Assume len(nums2) = n, n is even, 1 <= n <= 20000, and all array entries are between 1 and 1000000000.

statement: Let k = n/2, D1 = { nums1[i] | 0 <= i < n }, and D2 = { nums2[i] | 0 <= i < n }. Whenever maximum_set_size returns r, we have r >= max(min(k, |D1|), min(k, |D2|)).
preconditions: Let n = len(nums1). Assume len(nums2) = n, n is even, 1 <= n <= 20000, and all array entries are between 1 and 1000000000.

statement: Let D1 = { nums1[i] | 0 <= i < n } and D2 = { nums2[i] | 0 <= i < n }. Whenever maximum_set_size returns r, we have r >= |D1 ∩ D2|.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums1). Assume len(nums2) = n, n is even, 1 <= n <= 20000, and all array entries are between 1 and 1000000000.

statement: Swapping the two input arrays does not change the answer: maximum_set_size(nums1, nums2) and maximum_set_size(nums2, nums1) return the same result.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums1). Assume len(nums2) = n, n is even, 1 <= n <= 20000, and all array entries are between 1 and 1000000000.

statement: If nums1' is any permutation of nums1 and nums2' is any permutation of nums2, then maximum_set_size(nums1', nums2') returns the same result as maximum_set_size(nums1, nums2).
preconditions: Let n = len(nums1). Assume len(nums2) = n, n is even, 1 <= n <= 20000, and all array entries are between 1 and 1000000000.

statement: Whenever maximum_set_size returns r, there exist subsets I1 and I2 of {0, 1, ..., n-1}, each of size k = n/2, such that |{ nums1[i] | 0 <= i < n and i not in I1 } ∪ { nums2[i] | 0 <= i < n and i not in I2 }| = r.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums1). Assume len(nums2) = n, n is even, 1 <= n <= 20000, and all array entries are between 1 and 1000000000.

statement: Whenever maximum_set_size returns r, for every pair of subsets I1 and I2 of {0, 1, ..., n-1} with |I1| = |I2| = k = n/2, we have |{ nums1[i] | 0 <= i < n and i not in I1 } ∪ { nums2[i] | 0 <= i < n and i not in I2 }| <= r.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums1). Assume len(nums2) = n, n is even, 1 <= n <= 20000, and all array entries are between 1 and 1000000000.

statement: Then maximum_set_size(nums1', nums2') and maximum_set_size(nums1, nums2) return the same result; changing multiplicities without changing the two distinct-value sets does not change the answer.

Let D1 = { nums1[i] | 0 <= i < n } and D2 = { nums2[i] | 0 <= i < n }. Let nums1' and nums2' be arrays of length n with entries in the same range and with distinct-value sets D1' = D1 and D2' = D2.

statement: If maximum_set_size(nums1, nums2) returns r and maximum_set_size(nums1', nums2') returns r', then r <= r'.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums1). Assume len(nums2) = n, n is even, 1 <= n <= 20000, and all entries are between 1 and 1000000000. Let D1, D2 be the distinct-value sets of nums1, nums2. Let nums1', nums2' be arrays of length n with entries in the same range and distinct-value sets D1', D2'. Assume D1 ⊆ D1' and D2 ⊆ D2'.
